verses.text: After David had settled into his palace, he said to the prophet Nathan, "Look, I am living in a palace made of cedar, but the ark of the LORD's covenant is in a tent."
Nathan told David, "Do whatever you have in mind, because God is with you."
But that same night God's word came to Nathan. God said,
"Go and tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD says: You are not the one who will build me a house to live in.
I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel out of Egypt until today. I have moved from one tent to another and from one dwelling place to another.
Wherever I have moved with all Israel, did I ever ask any of the leaders I commanded to shepherd my people, "Why have you not built me a house of cedar?"'
So now, tell my servant David, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be the ruler over my people Israel.
I have been with you wherever you have gone, and I have destroyed all your enemies in front of you. Now I will make your name as famous as the names of the greatest men on earth.

I will provide a place for my people Israel and plant them there, so they can live in their own home and never be disturbed again. Wicked people will no longer crush them, as they did at the beginning,
and as they did from the time I appointed leaders over my people Israel. I will defeat all your enemies. I tell you that the LORD will build a house for you, a family line of kings.
When your life is over and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up one of your descendants, one of your own sons, to take your place. I will make his kingdom strong.
He is the one who will build a house for me, and I will make his throne last forever.
I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will never take my faithful love away from him, as I took it away from the king who ruled before you.
I will put him in charge of my house and my kingdom forever. His throne will last forever.'"
Nathan told David everything the LORD had said in this vision.
Then King David went in and sat before the LORD. He said, "Who am I, LORD God, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far?
And as if this were not enough in your eyes, God, you have also spoken about the future of your servant's family. You have treated me as if I were a very important man, LORD God.
What more can I say to you for honouring your servant like this? You know your servant.
LORD, you have done this great thing for your servant's sake and because you wanted to. You have made all these great things known.
LORD, there is no one like you. There is no God except you, as we have heard with our own ears.

Is there any other nation on earth like your people Israel? God went out to rescue them to be his own people, and to make a name for yourself by doing great and wonderful things. You drove out nations ahead of your people, whom you rescued from Egypt.
You made your people Israel your very own forever, and you, LORD, became their God.
So now, LORD, let the promise you have made about your servant and his family stand forever. Do what you have promised.

Then your name will stand firm and be honoured forever. People will say, 'The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, is truly Israel's God!' And the family of your servant David will stand firm before you.
You, my God, have shown your servant that you will build a family line of kings for him. That is why your servant has found the courage to pray to you.
LORD, you are God! You have promised this good thing to your servant.
Now you have been pleased to bless your servant's family, so that it will continue forever before you. You, LORD, have blessed it, and it will be blessed forever."
